name: Fast Vulkan engines on Pixel 10 Pro (Parakeet + MOSS latency)

description: Baseline: phone_ms=10069 (PK med 2886: mel 26, enc 2612, dec 248; MOSS short 7183: enc+prefill 3675, dec 3280 @102.5ms/tok). Transcripts captured as gate baseline.

asi.baseline_note: Branch head 94230cf. Enc+prefill split missing from this run due to parse bug (fixed); moss enc+prefill=3675 from raw output
asi.hypothesis: Baseline measurement of branch head (PR #287, commit 94230cf): Parakeet medium 2886ms (enc 2612), MOSS short 7183ms (decode 3280, 102.5ms/tok)

description: PowerVR vendor defaults: tile 32,64,4,4 + gemv rows 8 (tuner mis-ranks on real workloads). phone_ms 10069→9363 (PK 2886→2529, enc 2612→2288; MOSS 7183→6834, decode 99.2ms/tok). Transcripts match.

asi.failed_variants: 1) added 32,64,4,4 to candidates only → tuner still picked 64,32 (synthetic ranks it 77.9 vs 82.1ms). 2) barrier-after-every-kernel + norm-interleave in tune recording → still 64,32 (96.7 vs 102.3). 3) M=256→293 (odd tail waves) → still 64,32. Synthetic isolated recordings cannot see the 2x real-workload difference.
asi.hypothesis: Autotuner mis-ranks tiles on PowerVR: synthetic tune picked 64,64,4,4→64,32; real workload wants 32,64,4,4 (2526 vs 2907 med on PK medium) and gemv rows 8
asi.next: Bigger structural items: encoder GEMM kernel itself (subgroup 128 paths), dispatch count reduction, MOSS decode bandwidth

description: PowerVR: f32 GEMM products by default (f16 unpack/pack overhead > full-rate-f32 savings). phone_ms 9363→9261 (PK enc 2288→2262, MOSS enc+prefill 3452→3403). Env STARLING_FAST_F16 still overrides.

asi.hypothesis: Packed-f16 products are a desktop optimization; PowerVR DXT has full-rate f32 so the unpack/pack overhead dominates — f32 products should win
asi.insight: F16MATH path costs ~3% on PowerVR encoders; f32 also strictly improves numerics (products accumulate in f32), so WER gate unaffected by construction

description: Coopmat investigation: driver advertises VK_KHR_cooperative_matrix but shader compiler SEGFAULTS on any coopmat instruction (minimal probe). Kept machinery dormant (STARLING_FAST_COOPMAT=1 opt-in), capability dump in verbose, host glslc preferred. Metric 9285 = thermal noise vs 9261 best (PK enc actually improved to ~2244).

asi.crash_bisect: coopMatStore→shared: crash; coopMatStore→buffer: crash; load+muladd+store: crash; minimal 16x16x16 f16 probe: crash. Compiler segfaults in spvcompiler::LLVMWriter::emitCooperativeMatrixOp regardless of op/storage/instruction mix
asi.driver_details: PowerVR DXT-48-1536, driver 0x00696bd0, api 1.4.317. Reports coopmat 16x16x16+64x16x16 for A/B=FLOAT16 C=FLOAT32, SINT8→SINT32, UINT8→UINT32, scope=3 (subgroup). Enabling vulkanMemoryModel feature did NOT help
asi.glslc_change_side_effect: host glslc 2026.3 now compiles ALL shaders (was NDK 2022.3) — different SPIR-V codegen for scalar kernels; PK enc slightly better (2243 vs 2262), MOSS within thermal noise
asi.hypothesis: VK_KHR_cooperative_matrix (hw f16 matmul) could lift the ~155 GFLOPS GEMM ceiling several fold
asi.next: Scalar-kernel improvements: BK=64 K-tiles (halve barriers), double-buffered tile loads, norm fusion. Revisit coopmat after a PowerVR driver update (probe: coop_probe.comp)

description: BK64 experiment: 64-deep K tiles in scalar GEMM measured WORSE on PowerVR (PK enc 2254→2677ms, -19%). Barriers not the bottleneck; kernel is issue-limited. Discarded (reverted).

asi.bug_found_and_fixed: first BK64 attempt had OOB shared writes ((BM)*(BK/8) bound instead of (BM/2)*(BK/8) row-pairs) — BK32 path corrupted too, encoder 2856ms; fixed bounds restored 2254ms
asi.hypothesis: BK=64 K-tiles halve in-shader barrier count and double compute per barrier → faster GEMM on PowerVR
asi.insight: Barriers between K-slices are NOT the bottleneck (GFLOPS flat ~155 at all M, BK64 worse). The scalar kernel is ALU/issue-limited: per k, 3 shared loads + 3 unpackHalf2x16 + 16 FMA per thread. Without hw matmul (coopmat broken on driver), big GEMM gains need fewer ALU ops per FMA or fewer bytes (int8 dot).
asi.next: Abandon scalar-GEMM micro-tuning; focus on MOSS decode (100ms/token, 11GB/s: lm_head bytes, dispatch count) and PK decoder/mel (CPU side), then norm fusion (fewer dispatches)

description: GEMV RSPLIT: pad workgroups to a full subgroup with parallel row slots (wg=lanes*RSPLIT). MOSS decode 3203→3060ms (95.6ms/tok), phone_ms 9285→9151. W4 K=1024 GEMV 7→13.6 GB/s isolated. Transcripts match; CPU-reference check added to micro probe.

asi.artifact_warning: initial micro '3.5x' was an artifact: local_size_x_id still pointed at LANES so rs>0 threads never ran — 3/4 of rows unwritten (bandwidth inflated 4x, model output broke). Fixed with dedicated WGS spec constant (id 6). Real isolated gain W4 K=1024: 7.0→13.6 GB/s (1.9x)
asi.hypothesis: PowerVR issues whole 128-lane subgroups; GEMV workgroups with lanes=K/32<128 threads waste issue slots → pad workgroup with RSPLIT parallel row slots
asi.instrument: STARLING_FAST_MICRO=bits,N,K[,reps[,rows]] now also verifies GPU vs CPU reference (rel err 0.00000 for W4/W8) — reusable correctness+bandwidth probe

description: PowerVR tile default 32,64,4,4 → 32,128,4,8 (full subgroup + BN=128 halves weight re-reads). phone_ms 9151→8812 (PK enc 2260→2029, MOSS enc+prefill 3404→3056; MOSS decode drift = thermal). Transcripts match. ALU probe: 500 GFLOPS peak vs 155 achieved → still 3x headroom.

asi.alu_probe: pure-FMA probe: ~500 GFLOPS peak (48-192 WGs); GEMM at 155 = 31% of ALU peak — kernel has headroom, not at the wall
asi.config_pattern: best GEMM configs have wg=128 (one PowerVR subgroup) AND BN>=64 (weight re-read amortization): 16,64,4,4 wg=64 → 3836; 64,32,4,4 wg=128 but BN=32 → 5525; 32,128,4,8 wg=128 BN=128 → 1992-2033 BEST; 48/192/256 variants worse (wave quantization)
asi.hypothesis: Tile 32,128,4,8 (wg=128, BN=128 → half the weight re-reads of 32,64) beats 32,64,4,4

description: GEMM shared-tile double-buffering (prefetch next K slice while computing): PK enc 2029→3118ms, 54% WORSE — doubled shared memory halves occupancy. Reverted.

asi.hypothesis: Shared-tile double-buffering hides load latency behind compute (classic GPU GEMM optimization)
asi.insight: On PowerVR occupancy beats latency hiding: doubling shared 10KB→20KB per WG cut resident workgroups and cost 54%. The 155-vs-500 GFLOPS gap is NOT fixable by prefetch scheduling on this GPU; would need less shared per FMA (bigger thread tiles hit register limits) or hw matmul (coopmat broken)

description: PK decoder two-thread GEMV split (persistent spin worker, row-split) + NEON quantize + decode-stage timing. decode 252→201ms (-20%), joint halved. phone_ms 8812→8615. Transcripts match (row split numerically identical).

asi.hypothesis: PK TDT decoder is single-threaded; splitting large GEMV rows across a persistent spin-sync worker thread halves the joint network time
asi.implementation: cpu::GemvHelper: one worker spinning on a seq counter, row-split (numerically identical), split when macs>1M; NEON/AVX2 quantize (nearest-even, saturating) also landed; per-stage decode timing under STARLING_PARAKEET_TIMING
asi.split_breakdown: joint 106→57-67ms, pred 138→124ms, decode total 252→201ms; argmax +3ms (thread contention)

description: Verification rerun: phone_ms 8874 (warm phone; PK stable at ~2288, MOSS decode thermal drift). Session best stands at 8615 (-14.4% vs baseline).

asi.hypothesis: Verification rerun of kept state (4be985e) after energy measurements warmed the phone
asi.note: MOSS decode 3337 vs 3050 in the kept run = thermal drift; PK stable (2288 vs 2293). No code change since last keep.

description: Adaptive GEMV rows: grow rows for large N (while N/rows≥384, cap 32) to amortize x re-reads; env pins rows exactly. MOSS decode 3050→2821ms (88.2ms/tok), phone_ms 8615→8358.8. Desktop unchanged. Reduction order row-independent → transcripts identical.

asi.exact_shapes: MOSS LLM: hidden 2048, 28 layers, ffn 6144 → ff_up N=12288 K=2048 W4; lm_head N=151936 K=2048 (Q8, 3 chunks). Micro (rows sweep, isolated): ff_up 8:14.9 16:15.8 32:17.4 48:15.0 64:13.6 GB/s — 48+ regresses (register pressure with RPP=rows/rsplit)
asi.hypothesis: At rows=8 every GEMV workgroup re-reads the whole x vector once; for large-N matrices (ff_up 12.6MB x vs 15.7MB weights, lm_head reads x 19k times) the x traffic rivals the weights — grow rows adaptively for large N
asi.premise_flip: The original global rows sweep (rows=16/32 worse) predated the RSPLIT fix; with subgroup-padded workgroups the landscape flipped (rows=16 decode 2606 vs 3040ms at 8). Per-shape rule beats both globals.

description: MOSS mel experiment: persistent thread pool + hypot→sqrt both failed (pool: no win, E-core gating; sqrt: flipped fixture transcript, gate 1). Reverted both. mel stays ~170ms, documented as numerics-pinned.

asi.hypothesis: MOSS mel is 20-40x slower on phone vs desktop; suspected per-call thread spawn (parallel_for spawns+joins 9 threads per loop) and/or std::hypot (slow on bionic)
asi.mel_anatomy: per-frame ~167µs single-threaded on phone (desktop per-thread ~78µs = normal 2x CPU gap). PkMel does equivalent math at 11µs/frame with sqrt + hand-rolled FFT
asi.result_1: persistent parked pool (fixed-slot, tid-preserving): no win — 4thr 166ms vs 1thr 124ms; big.LITTLE join-gating dominates, parallelism never pays for this size
asi.result_2_gate_violation: hypot→double sqrt flipped the fixture transcript ('well, i don't wish'→'Don't wish', 32→28 tokens) — 1-ulp mel differences move near-tie tokens. REVERTED. The mel is numerics-pinned to ggml's exact path; any speedup must keep hypot or re-baseline transcripts+WER together
asi.next_action_hint: mel speedup only viable as a deliberate numerics change with FLEURS re-gate, or GPU mel with bit-matching; both are separate efforts

description: GEMM uvec2 wide shared loads in the f32 product loop: PK enc 2082-2095 vs 2058-2066 baseline — neutral. glslc already merges adjacent loads. Reverted.

asi.hypothesis: GEMM inner loop issues 6 shared transactions per k (4 B + 2 A unpacks); explicit uvec2 wide loads (3 transactions) would lift the shared-bandwidth ceiling
asi.insight: PK encoder 2082-2095ms vs 2058-2066 baseline — neutral/slightly worse. glslc already coalesces adjacent uint loads, or shared transaction count is not the limiter. The scalar GEMM is at a structural local optimum: tile sweep won, BK64/double-buffer/wide-loads all neutral-or-worse; remaining 3x-to-ALU-peak needs hw matmul (coopmat broken on driver 00696bd0)

description: Mel filterbank sparsity: per-mel nonzero [lo,hi) bin ranges (PkMel-style), bit-exact zero skipping + STARLING_MEL_TIMING phase instrumentation. MOSS mel 200→131ms, filterbank 82-100→12-14ms (7x). phone_ms 8358.8→8319.1. Transcripts identical; desktop mel 6.5→3.2ms.

asi.gate_safety: skipping exact-zero filterbank terms is bit-identical (products are >= +0.0 and x+0.0==x); transcripts byte-identical on phone; desktop mel 6.5->3.2ms, MOSS total unchanged (1782ms, decode variance)
asi.hypothesis: mel timing breakdown (new STARLING_MEL_TIMING): filterbank loop was 61-100ms of MOSS mel because it multiplies all 201 spectral bins per (mel,frame) while triangular mel filters are ~2/3 zeros; PkMel-style per-mel [lo,hi) ranges skip them
asi.mel_phases_now: fft ~70ms (thread-noisy; ~40ms single-thread real work), filterbank 12-14ms (was 82-100), log+norm ~32ms (95K log10 f64, numerics-pinned). Remaining mel cost is the FFT loop; deeper cuts need numerics changes (gated)
asi.side_findings: subgroup-shuffle norm rewrite was 4x SLOWER on PowerVR (falsified, reverted); 1-thread mel only ~50ms better and scheduler-noisy — left default

description: dec_attn investigation: measured 3.9-4.2ms/token via new attn micro probe; barrier-fusion and load-prefetch variants both falsified (neutral-to-worse — kernel is latency-dominated at 16 WGs, not barrier/loop bound). Reverted. attn probe + scaling analysis documented.

asi.attn_anatomy: attn_decode = 3.9-4.2ms/token at pos~100 (4.4% of decode), scaling to 26.6ms/token at pos=1000. Only ~16µs/token is FLOPs; the dispatch has just 16 head-workgroups (2048 threads) — latency-dominated end to end
asi.falsified_1: vec2 q+k stats fusion + max-scan (barriers 30→16): 0.151→0.158ms/dispatch, WORSE at high pos (max-scan adds O(pos) shared reads). Barriers already overlap across the 16 head workgroups
asi.falsified_2: rolling depth-4 prefetch in the value-mix loop (add order preserved, bit-exact): 0.157ms — neutral. Loads were already pipelined by compiler/hardware
asi.hypothesis: dec_attn's 28 in-shader barrier trees / dependent V-load chain dominate its 4ms/token — either could be removed deterministically
asi.instrument: STARLING_FAST_MICRO=attn[,pos[,reps[,maxpos]]] probe added (measures one layer's fused attention at real shape H=16 KVH=4 D=128)
asi.scaling_probe: MOSS enc+prefill vs audio length: 3130ms(T=743) → 7366ms(T=2230) = 2.85ms/frame + ~1.0s fixed; encoder at ~227 GFLOPS = at the GEMM wall, no hidden pathology

description: Verification: phone_ms 8143 (PK 2184: enc 1974, dec 172; MOSS 5959: mel 83, enc+prefill 2955, decode 88.5ms/tok). Session best; transcripts match.

asi.hypothesis: Verification rerun of kept state (13d2d06) after the falsified attn experiments were reverted — cool phone
asi.note: Best composite of the session: PK enc 1974 ( coolest yet), MOSS 5959 total. Confirms the kept state is healthy and the attn discards reverted cleanly.

description: lm_head W4 requant (convert_w8_w4 + STARLING_FAST_LM4=1): works (identical transcripts, −149MB, isolated 8% faster lm_head) but net 0.9% of decode = sub-noise at composite; not worth the FLEURS gate cost. Discarded (machinery documented for future).

asi.future_lever: STARLING_FAST_LM4=1 exists and works: identical fixtures, -149MB memory, load ~0.3s faster, lm_head 8% faster isolated. Flip default only if a FLEURS run is done (numerics: near-tie argmax over requantized table) AND the product values the memory/load more than gate cost
asi.hypothesis: Q8 tied lm_head (28% of decode bytes per brief) → requantize to W4 at load; halved bytes should cut ~6ms/token
asi.measured_reality: isolated lm_head GEMV: W8 already runs at 36.6 GB/s (9.57ms), W4 at 22.1 GB/s (8.78ms) — W4's higher ALU-per-byte caps its bandwidth, net saving only 0.79ms/token = 25ms/fixture = 0.9% decode, below the ±0.5% composite noise floor
asi.verification: requant verified correct: weights 1612→1463 MiB, embed W4 2 chunks, transcripts byte-identical on short

description: Verification: phone_ms 8140.9 (session best 8143 confirmed within noise). PK 2214 (enc 1989), MOSS 5927 (decode 88.9ms/tok). Transcripts match.

asi.hypothesis: Post-revert health check of the kept state (c622612) — confirms the lm4 discard reverted cleanly and the composite holds
asi.note: 8140.9 confirms 8143 session best within ±0.03%; all gates green.

description: Repack disk cache (PackCache: fingerprint, mmap carve, parallel pwrite, atomic publish — fully working, transcripts identical): measured NET LOSS on this phone. Cold +4.9s (MOSS, flash write ~200MB/s), warm 2134 vs 1324ms repack (1.6GB doesn't fit page cache). The parallel repack is already storage-speed. Reverted; design documented for revival on faster storage.

asi.flash_speeds: Pixel 10 Pro storage: ~200MB/s parallel-pwrite, ~0.8-1.5GB/s read. Repack compute: parallel ~1.2GB/s for MOSS (1.6GB in 1.3s). The CPU repack is ALREADY storage-speed on this device
asi.future_note: Cache becomes attractive on desktop/NVMe or if the app ever repacks slower than I/O (e.g. single-threaded). Design validated end-to-end (fingerprint, mmap carve, atomic publish); documented for revival
asi.hypothesis: Brief's load-time idea: 'cache the repacked blob on disk (mmap) to skip repacking entirely on later loads' — assumes repack >> I/O
asi.implementation: full PackCache built and verified correct: content fingerprint (shapes+types+sampled bytes), mmap parallel carve, offset-reserved parallel pwrite, atomic .tmp rename; transcripts identical warm and cold; cache sizes 610MB (PK) / 1.6GB (MOSS)
asi.measured_reality: PK: cold+write 3320ms (vs 455 repack baseline), warm 320-345ms — page-cache dependent. MOSS: cold 6197ms (vs 1324), warm 2134ms — WORSE than repack even warm (1.6GB doesn't fit page cache; flash reads ~0.8GB/s at scale). Net loss at both scales
asi.rollback_reason: cold load regression +4.9s (MOSS) / +2.9s (PK); warm MOSS still -0.8s worse than baseline repack

description: Verification after PackCache revert: phone_ms 8331 (thermal band; session best 8143 with identical code). Transcripts match, all reverts clean.

asi.hypothesis: Post-revert health check after the PackCache discard (warm phone this time)
asi.note: 8331 vs session best 8143: within the ±2% thermal band seen all session (identical code). Gates green. Upload observation for the backlog: mapped upload measured 570-800MB/s across sessions (parallel already; possible per-blob flush cost if non-coherent — unverified).
